title: DDIA 10 · BATCH PROCESSING
subtitle: Take a big, bounded, immutable input, run a pure function over it, and produce a derived output.
footer: Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann). Read the book.

blocks.text: Sort by count and take the top 5. Six tiny programs, composed through one uniform interface: a stream of lines.
Each reducer sees all values for its keys together, aggregates them, and writes output files. If a task fails, just rerun that task, because inputs are immutable.
Broadcast hash join: if one side is small (a hotel dimension table), load it into each mapper's memory. No shuffle is needed.
Dataflow engines run the whole workflow as one DAG and pipeline data between operators.

items: The frontier queue feeds fetchers. Text extraction and dedup run as batch (Spark) over S3. Re-runnable because raw pages are stored immutably.
Nightly batch over the event log in S3 or the warehouse. The streaming path gives fast approximate results and batch gives exact ones (Ch 12, Lambda).
"How do you rebuild the search index?"
Batch-build a new index from the source of truth, then atomically switch the alias. Old index kept for rollback.

blocks.text: "Raw events land immutably in S3, partitioned by date. Any derived table can be recomputed from them, which is our safety net for bugs."
